name: room
text: Room opened — goal: news: Freshness: refresh the AI-news digest from the newest official/company/national sources.

name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the freshest AI-news from the last 24 h: run `curl -s https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent | grep -o 'arxiv.org/abs/[0-9.]*' | sort -u > arxiv-links.txt` (≈120 new papers), then fetch each abstract with `parallel -j8 'curl -sL https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id={} | grep -oPm1 "<title>.*?</title>" >> arxiv-titles.txt'`, and finally append today’s company/national announcements scraped from `https://ai.googleblog.com/feed`, `https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/feed/`, and `https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news` to `official-ai-news.txt`.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** The proposal risks *false precision*—`grep -oPm1 "<title>.*"` is brittle; arXiv’s API returns malformed XML (e.g., unescaped `&` in titles) that breaks the regex. Evidence: test with `curl -sL https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id=2406.12345`—you’ll see titles like `"Attention & Transformers"` fail. Demand a proper XML parser (e.g., `xmlstarlet` or Python’s `feedparser`) to avoid silent data loss.
